title: -ing form or infinitive
subtitle: prefer, would rather, had better, infinitives of purpose

blocks.text: Some verb, noun and adjective phrases are usually followed by the **-ing** form. I've **finished writing** my essay.
Some of the verbs, nouns and adjectives in the list above can also be followed by an object before the **-ing** form.
blocks.note: I can't **stand people cheating** in exams.

items: When we put a verb after a preposition, we almost always use an **-ing** form.
I'm interested **in hearing** more about that course.

theory.title: verb / noun / adjective phrase + full infinitive

blocks.text: Some verb, noun and adjective phrases are usually followed by the full infinitive. Your answer **appears to be** wrong.
Some of the verbs, nouns and adjectives in the list above can also be followed by an object before the full infinitive.
blocks.note: I didn't **want to take** the exam. · My mum didn't **want me to take** the exam.

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by an object + the bare infinitive. You never **let me say** the answer.

The verbs **feel, hear, notice, see** and **watch** can also be followed by the **-ing** form. We often use the bare infinitive for a completed action (from start to finish). We often use the **-ing** form for an action in progress at the time.
blocks.note: I **heard** Miss Jenkins **tell** Julie not to do that. (= I heard all of it.) · I **heard** Miss Jenkins **telling** Julie not to do that. (= I heard part of it.)

items: In the passive, **hear, make** and **see** are followed by the full infinitive.
Active: The teacher **made me stand** in the corner.
Passive: I **was made to stand** in the corner.

theory.title: full infinitive or -ing with little or no change

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by the full infinitive or the **-ing** form with little or no change in meaning. We **continued to do** experiments in the lab all afternoon. · We **continued doing** experiments in the lab all afternoon.

theory.title: full infinitive or -ing with a change in meaning

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by both the full infinitive and the **-ing** form. The choice depends on the meaning. I **remember** teachers at my school **hitting** children when they were naughty! · Did you **remember to do** your homework?

items: **remember / forget + -ing**: a memory of the past. **remember / forget + infinitive**: something you need to do.
**stop + -ing**: quit an activity. **stop + infinitive**: pause in order to do something else.
**regret + -ing**: be sorry about the past. **regret + infinitive**: be sorry about what you are about to say.
**go on + -ing**: continue. **go on + infinitive**: move on to the next thing.

rows.use: prefer + noun / -ing + to + noun / -ing · general preference
rows.example: I **prefer** biology **to** history. · I **prefer reading** English texts **to speaking** in English.

rows.use: would prefer + full infinitive + rather than (+ bare / full infinitive) · specific preference
rows.example: I'd **prefer to have** the lesson on Wednesday **rather than (to) have** it on Tuesday, if that's possible.

rows.use: would rather + bare infinitive + than (+ bare infinitive) · specific preference
rows.example: I'd **rather have** the lesson on Wednesday **than (have it)** on Tuesday, if that's possible.

rows.use: would rather + subject + past simple / past continuous · preference about someone else
rows.example: I'd **rather you didn't sit** next to Brian.

rows.use: had better + bare infinitive · giving advice
rows.example: You'd **better ask** your parents if you can come on the school trip.

blocks.text: We don't usually say **I don't prefer…**. We use **I prefer not to…**.
blocks.note: I **prefer not to** have music on when I'm studying.

blocks.text: When we want to talk about someone's purpose (the reason they do something), we can use the full infinitive, **in order** + full infinitive, or **so as** + full infinitive.

rows.example: I went to university **to avoid getting** a job.
I went to university **in order to avoid getting** a job.
I went to university **so as to avoid getting** a job.

blocks.text: We can also express the same idea using **so (that)**.
blocks.note: I went to university **so (that) I could avoid getting** a job.

blocks.text: With a negative purpose we don't normally use the full infinitive on its own.
blocks.note: I went to university **in order not to get** a job. · I went to university **so as not to get** a job. (not *I went to university not to get a job.*)

blocks.correct: I went to university **so as not to get** a job.
blocks.incorrect: I went to university **not to get** a job.

exercises.title: E · Same meaning or different?
exercises.instruction: For each pair, choose whether both sentences mean the same thing or have different meanings.

items.prompt: a I can't bear being tickled! · b I can't bear to be tickled!
a My boss went on saying that he was very proud of all of us. · b My boss went on to say that he was very proud of all of us.
a Have you stopped having lunch yet? · b Have you stopped to have lunch yet?
a Have you started having lunch yet? · b Have you started to have lunch yet?
a They continued climbing the mountain. · b They continued to climb the mountain.
a We all saw the reporter interviewing the witness. · b We all saw the reporter interview the witness.
